In Saints Row: The Third, players can participate in various activities, some of which were introduced in previous Saints Row games. These activities serve the plot, acting as training for the player-character or causing damage to the Syndicate. They can also be repeated. Outside of structured diversions, the player can explore the open world and engage in various criminal activities.

The "Maximum Mayhem" activities are a series of destructive challenges where players maximize property destruction before a time expires. Some of these diversions were introduced in previous Saints Row games. Activities serve the plot and are positioned as training the player-character or damaging the Syndicate. They can also be repeated.

In addition to the in-game activities, the Saints Row franchise is also associated with a literary past. The name "Saints Row" is derived from the title of two occasional poems published as broadsides and signed "M.M.", though the source texts have been lost.
